subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: The River Styx
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The River Styx.

hook.text: The Styx separated the living from the dead. Swearing by the Styx was the most unbreakable oath for Greek gods.

buildup.text: Achilles was dipped in the Styx as a baby—making him invulnerable except where his mother held his heel.

discovery.text: Five rivers in Hades: Styx for hate, Acheron for woe, Lethe for forgetting, Phlegethon for fire, Cocytus for grief.

twist.text: The Styx was a real stream in Greece. A poisonous waterfall in Arcadia may have inspired the myth.

climax.text: The Styx proves that rivers as boundaries endure in language: 'crossing the Rubicon' echoes the same mythic logic.

punchline.text: Cross it once. There's no coming back.

quiz.question: What made an oath sworn by the Styx special?
options: It was the most unbreakable oath even for gods
